item.title: Jana Riess: New book aims to break silence on LDS temple garments
item.description: The LDS Church and most members are getting more comfortable talking about temple garments. But some holdouts prefer the old days of silence and secrecy.

item.title: A Utah Republican and a California Democrat are teaming up to take on sports gambling on prediction markets
item.description: Utah Sen. John Curtis is sponsoring the bipartisan “Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act.”

item.title: People in handcuffs boarded a plane at Salt Lake City’s airport. Was it an ICE flight? Here’s what we know.
item.description: Were people in handcuffs Monday at Salt Lake City International Airport being transported by ICE? Here's what we know.

item.title: Voices: In Iran, the U.S. faces a classic case of alliance entrapment. Here’s how Utah and federal leaders can avoid it.
item.description: “U.S. policymakers can effectively pressure leaders to enter peace negotiations, even when concessions are viewed by the public as costly,” writes Utah State University professor Austin Knuppe in an op-ed.

item.title: Voices: Why expanded roles for Latter-day Saint women still stop short of equality
item.description: “If progress is to feel meaningful, it must extend beyond presence into authority, into the ability to shape outcomes, not simply support them,” writes Diana Wilson in an op-ed.

item.title: Why Utah football won’t have its 22 Forever spring game this year
item.description: The Utes are planning something different this spring.

item.title: Will giving the Rio Grande Depot to the U. create more hurdles for a development plan?
item.description: In the closing days of the legislative session, lawmakers gave the historic Rio Grande Depot to the University of Utah. Will that hurt the Rio Grande Plan?

item.description: Opinion: The war is going better than you think

item.title: Opinion: America has become a dangerous nation
item.description: We had a good run — some eight decades or so — but it is clear by now that the United States has ceased to be the leader of the free world. A successor for that post has not been named, and it appears unlikely that the European Union, or NATO, or whatever constitutes “the West” these days will promote from within. The job might even be eliminated, one more reduction in force, courtesy of President Donald Trump.

item.title: ‘The situation is dire’: Lake Powell is heading for a record low as Colorado River states remain deadlocked
item.description: After a record low snowpack, Colorado River states face a near-term crisis at Lake Powell and an ongoing stalemate over longterm plans. "The stakes have never been higher," said one state negotiator.

item.title: Are March Madness Cinderellas dead? Jerrod Calhoun’s Utah State exit shines a light on a harsh reality.
item.description: Can any coach build a real tournament contender at Utah State? Jerrod Calhoun’s departure provides his answer.

item.title: Letter: The effects of air pollution in the Salt Lake Valley are ominous. There are some ways to mitigate exposure.
item.description: Letter: The time for sugarcoating has long passed. When it comes to addressing the lethality of air pollution, public health officials and lawmakers have turned their backs on us.

item.title: Petroglyph vandalism near Moab under investigation
item.description: The Grand County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help after ancient petroglyphs were vandalized at a recreation area near Tusher Tunnel west of Moab.

item.title: Letter: Is the Trump administration’s war of choice against Iran the prelude to Armageddon?
item.description: Letter: The repercussions of Donald Trump and Bibi Netanyahu's war in Iran are already proving far greater than either man anticipated.

item.title: Voices: For many, Great Salt Lake’s decline feels distant. I’ve witnessed its collapse in a way few others have.
item.description: “I hope to someday be recruited as a D1 rower,” writes Katherine Parker in an op-ed. “But if Great Salt Lake’s water levels continue to fall, my teammates and I will have nowhere to train, and future Utahns will miss out on any chance to row.”
